answers.stem_only: The backend, using its own IAM role credentials, generates a presigned PUT URL for a single object key with a short expiry and returns it to the app; the app uploads directly to S3. No long-term credentials in the app, no public bucket.
Replication rules only cover objects written after the rule exists; use S3 Batch Replication (a Batch Operations job tied to the replication rule) to replicate the existing objects.

Turn on S3 Block Public Access at the account level (all four settings, in particular BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets); it covers all current and future buckets and only the security team can change it.
Use multipart upload: the file is sent as parts that can upload in parallel, and a failed part is retried alone instead of the whole 2 TB object.
Turn on S3 Versioning so deletes create delete markers and overwrites keep the prior version; add a lifecycle rule to expire noncurrent versions after some days to control cost.

Turn on S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket and have clients use the accelerate endpoint, routing uploads through the nearest edge location over the AWS network (with multipart upload for large files).

S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a bucket default retention period of 7 years; compliance mode cannot be bypassed or shortened by any user, including root, and the default retention needs no application change.
SSE-C: the client supplies its own key with each PUT and GET over HTTPS; S3 encrypts and decrypts with it and does not store the key (only a salted HMAC to validate).

Cross-account access needs both sides: a bucket policy statement in account A that allows s3:GetObject to the Lambda execution role ARN, and an identity-based policy on the execution role in account B that allows s3:GetObject on those objects. SSE-S3 needs no KMS key policy change.

S3 event notifications cannot target an SQS FIFO queue directly. Turn on Amazon EventBridge for the bucket and create a rule for Object Created events that targets the FIFO queue (with a message group ID); no code needed.

Create an S3 access point restricted to the analytics VPC (network origin VPC) with its own access point policy granting the analytics role read access; the bucket policy already delegates to access points, so it and the other teams are unchanged.
Re-creatable, infrequently accessed data needing millisecond access: S3 One Zone-IA (lower price than Standard-IA; single AZ is acceptable because the data can be regenerated).

One lifecycle rule: S3 Standard for 30 days, transition to S3 Standard-IA at day 30 (multi-AZ, ms access), transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive at day 90 (standard retrieval within 12 hours), expire after 7 years.
Enable Requester Pays on the bucket and grant the partner accounts read access; the requesters pay the request and data transfer charges.

Objects of 20 KB are poor candidates for IA classes (128 KB minimum billable size, per-object transition costs; Intelligent-Tiering does not auto-tier objects under 128 KB). Since a day's results are read together, aggregate them into one large object per day and then transition that object to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days.
Infrequent (monthly) access, millisecond retrieval, must survive an AZ loss, only copy: S3 Standard-IA.
Unknown or changing access patterns with objects larger than 128 KB: S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which moves each object between access tiers automatically with no retrieval fees.
S3 Glacier Deep Archive (lowest storage price) and restore requested recordings with the Bulk retrieval option, which completes within 48 hours and is the cheapest restore.
S3 Object Lock in governance mode with a bucket default retention of 7 years; grant only the security team s3:BypassGovernanceRetention so it can remove the protection when needed.
Client-side encryption: encrypt each object in the data center with the on-premises key before upload and decrypt after download; AWS never sees plaintext or the key.
Long-lived data accessed about once a quarter that needs millisecond retrieval: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.

Add lifecycle actions: NoncurrentVersionExpiration to permanently delete versions 30 days after they become noncurrent, and AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload to remove parts of uploads not completed within some days.
